qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Scarce entitled infill locations and local municipal zoning restrict new open-air retail development, but Kimco lacks pricing power above inflation and fails the proof-of-moat capital return test. 5-year median ROIC is ~2.2%, well below the 12% threshold, with contractual 1.5-3.0% rent escalators constrained by tenant occupancy costs.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3b (ROIC = 2.2%, REJECT). While Kimco owns high-quality grocery-anchored shopping centers on scarce infill suburban land, retail real estate generates structurally sub-hurdle returns on capital (5Y median ROIC ~2.2% vs. 12% threshold). Contractual lease escalators are modest and pricing power is constrained by tenant retail economics, failing Charlie Munger's proof-of-moat standard.
qualitative.evidence: 5-year median GAAP ROIC is ~2.2% (FY20: 1.94%, FY21: 1.54%, FY22: 2.12%, FY23: 2.42%, FY24: 2.12%, FY25: 2.60%), with 10-year median ROIC of 4.8%, far below the 12% minimum hurdle. Total debt stands at ~$8.86B against FY25 net income of $592.8M and FFO of ~$1.2B, reflecting real estate leverage required to support low asset yields. Significant acquisitive expansion (RPT Realty $2.0B all-stock acquisition in 2024, Weingarten in 2021) expands gross leasable area across Coastal/Sunbelt hubs but fails to overcome structural real estate capital intensity and thin tenant spread economics.
